findings.issue: The model contract gate accepts impossible prediction responses: reviewer MockTransport returned prediction=999, omitted class_name, probabilities={cultivar_1:-1,cultivar_2:2}, and the probe passed. A second response with prediction=true and NaN probability also passed. The model load gate only checks status and version, so similarly invalid responses under load count as successes. This fails closed-release contract semantics.
findings.suggestion: Use one strict prediction response validator for baseline, rollback and every load response: exact supported class mapping, strict integer prediction, matching class_name, expected probability keys, finite numeric values in [0,1], normalized sum, and expected version. Add negative regression probes.

findings.issue: Cleanup only signals the group while its leader is alive. Reviewer started an owned parent that spawned a 30-second child in the inherited owned process group and exited; stop_all left child PID 44056 alive and emptied owned_names. Reviewer terminated that child explicitly. A leader exit therefore silently loses an owned descendant and can leave ports/resources running.
findings.suggestion: Retain ownership until the owned group is verified gone; handle exited leaders and TERM-ignoring descendants without signaling unrelated/reused process identities. Add a regression covering leader exit and an external sentinel that remains alive.
